vitehubFinanceIsOpenSourceSoftwareThatAP: ViteHub Finance is open-source software that a person or household runs for themselves. Whoever runs this copy, the operator, holds your data. This page covers what it keeps, where, and who can see it.
yourNameEmailAndSignInDetailsAHashedPass: Your name, email, and sign-in details: a hashed password, passkeys, your two-factor secret, and active sessions (with their IP address and browser).
theAccountsYouConnectOrAddBalancesTransa: The accounts you connect or add: balances, transactions, holdings, and what you add to them (categories, notes, rules, budgets, goals, recurring payments).
howToReachEachConnectionABankSessionAnEx: How to reach each connection: a bank session, an exchange’s API key, an Interactive Brokers Flex token, or a wallet address.
apiKeysYouCreateAndTheAgentsMcpClientsYo: API keys you create and the agents (MCP clients) you approve.
logsForFindingAndFixingErrorsEachRequest: Logs, for finding and fixing errors: each request’s page or API path, timing, and outcome, with your user and household ids but never your name, email, or transaction details; and errors your browser hits, with the page’s path (no query) and the error message. On Cloudflare they’re kept for 3 to 7 days. On other hosts, the operator decides.
inThisInstanceSOwnDatabaseCloudflareD1Wh: In this instance’s own database: Cloudflare D1 when it runs on Cloudflare, or an SQLite file on the operator’s server. There is no central service. The ViteHub Finance project never receives your data.
aLicensedAccountInformationServiceProvid: , a licensed account information service provider under PSD2. You give consent on your bank’s own page. Access is read-only: balances and transactions, never payments. Consent lasts up to 180 days, and you can revoke it at any time by removing the connection here or at your bank.
exchangesConnectWithReadOnlyApiKeysYouCr: Exchanges connect with read-only API keys you create. Interactive Brokers connects with a Flex token that only reads reports. Wallets are public addresses, looked up on public blockchain services. Coin prices (CoinGecko) and exchange rates (the ECB, through Frankfurter) are fetched by currency and coin symbol only.
whenNoRuleCategorizesATransactionThisIns: When no rule categorizes a transaction, this instance asks
sJevModelToSuggestOneItSendsTheTransacti: ’s Jev model to suggest one. It sends the transaction’s description and payee, whether money went in or out, the amount rounded to two significant digits, the currency, the account type, and the household’s category names and rule keywords. Names of household members, IBANs, and long numbers (cards, accounts, references) are masked first. It never sends dates, balances, account names, or who you are. Suggestions are marked as such, and the household’s owner can turn this off in Settings.
bankSessionsExchangeKeysAndBrokerTokensA: Bank sessions, exchange keys, and broker tokens are encrypted at rest with AES-GCM, using a key only the server holds. Passwords are stored as hashes. The only cookies are for signing in. There are no ads, trackers, or analytics.
accountsSharedWithYourHouseholdAreVisibl: Accounts shared with your household are visible to its members. A private account is visible only to its owner, in every list, total, chart, API response, and agent tool. On a shared account, its owner can mark a single transaction “Only me”: the rest of the household doesn’t see it anywhere, though the account’s balance still includes it. Agents and API keys you connect see what you see. Your data is never sold or shared with anyone else, apart from the services this page names. If this instance sends email (invitations, sign-in links, consent reminders), those messages go through its email provider.
removingAConnectionEndsItsAccessAndDelet: Removing a connection ends its access and deletes its accounts and their history, unless you choose to keep them as manual accounts. Deleting an account deletes its transactions, balances, and holdings. Leaving a household takes your accounts with you. Delete account, in Settings, deletes your sign-in and your household with everything in it; if others share your household, leave it first.

catalogIbkrIntro: ViteHub Finance reads one report you set up in IBKR, once a day, with a token that can only fetch reports. Setting it up takes about five minutes in IBKR’s Client Portal.
catalogIbkrAiBody: On IBKR’s Flex Queries page, click Configure with AI and paste this prompt. Check that the query it builds has both sections and XML, then save.
catalogIbkrAiManual: Or set it up by hand
catalogIbkrSectionsRest: Leave every other section unticked: nothing else is read. Account Information can stay ticked.
catalogIbkrQueryDone: I saved the query and have its Query ID
catalogIbkrQueryDoneHelp: You paste the Query ID in the last step.
catalogIbkrQueryGuide: IBKR’s guide to Activity Flex Queries
catalogIbkrQueryStep1: Sign in to IBKR’s Client Portal and open Performance & Reports › Flex Queries.
catalogIbkrQueryStep2: Next to Activity Flex Query, click + and name the query, for example ViteHub Finance.
catalogIbkrQueryStep3: Under Sections, tick Open Positions and Cash Report, as listed above. In each, choose Select All for the fields, and Summary under Options for Open Positions.
catalogIbkrQueryStep4: Under Delivery Configuration, set Format to XML and Period to Last Business Day. Leave General Configuration and Filters as they are, with Display Account Alias and Breakout by Day on No, then Continue and save.
catalogIbkrQueryStep5: Then open the query’s info (the i next to it) and note its Query ID, a number.
catalogIbkrQuerySummary: Create an Activity Flex Query with Open Positions and Cash Report, in XML. It decides what ViteHub Finance reads.
catalogIbkrTokenStep1: On the same Flex Queries page, open Flex Web Service Configuration (the gear next to Flex Web Service).
catalogIbkrTokenStep2: Turn the Flex Web Service on.
catalogIbkrTokenStep3: Generate a new token. Leave “Valid For IP Address” empty, since this server has no fixed address, and pick the longest expiry.
catalogIbkrTokenStep4: Copy the token. Generating another one later replaces it.
catalogIbkrTokenSummary: Turn on the Flex Web Service and generate a token. It fetches your Flex Queries and nothing else: no trading, no transfers.

demoPrivacyIntro: This is the demo of ViteHub Finance, an open-source app. Its household, people, banks, and transactions are made up.
demoPrivacyNoAccounts: There’s no sign-up here. You browse as one of the demo’s people, so this site keeps no name, email, password, or financial data of yours. A cookie keeps you in the demo while you browse.
demoPrivacyShared: Everyone shares the demo, so what you change there, like a category or a note, is visible to other visitors until it resets every night. Don’t type personal information into it.
demoPrivacyLogs: To find and fix errors, the server logs each request: the page, the time, and any error. Cloudflare keeps these logs for a few days.
demoTermsIntro: This is a demo of ViteHub Finance, open-source software, for trying it out. Everything in it is made up.
demoTermsAsIs: It’s provided as is, with no warranty. It can change, reset, or go offline at any time.
demoTermsUse: Don’t enter personal or real financial data, and don’t try to break or overload it.
